domain_entities.name: LeaveRequest
domain_entities.purpose: Represents an employee's leave application. Tracks the full lifecycle from draft through submission, approval/rejection, and optional cancellation. References the employee, the leave type/policy, and the approving/rejecting manager.
lifecycle_states: DRAFT — initial state; employee is composing the request; not yet visible to managers; editable by the employee
SUBMITTED — employee has submitted for review; visible to the manager; no longer editable by the employee; transition: submit()
APPROVED — manager has approved the leave; balance is deducted; transition: approve(managerId)
REJECTED — manager has rejected the leave; balance is unaffected; transition: reject(managerId, reason)
CANCELLED — leave was cancelled; if previously APPROVED, balance is restored; if DRAFT or SUBMITTED, no balance impact; terminal state; transition: cancel(actorId)

domain_entities.name: LeaveType
domain_entities.purpose: Enumeration of leave categories. The feature focuses on annual, sick, and emergency, but the domain accommodates unpaid, maternity, and paternity for extensibility.

domain_entities.name: LeavePolicy
domain_entities.purpose: Defines the rules and entitlements for a specific leave type. Each policy governs how many days an employee is entitled to, whether manager approval is required, minimum notice periods, and accrual behaviour. One policy per leave type (annual, sick, emergency, etc.).
lifecycle_states: ACTIVE — policy is in effect; leave requests can reference it; transition: activate()
INACTIVE — policy is disabled; no new leave requests can use this policy; existing approved leaves are unaffected; transition: deactivate()

domain_entities.name: LeaveBalance
domain_entities.purpose: Tracks an employee's leave entitlement, usage, and remaining balance for a specific leave policy within a fiscal year. Deducted when leave is approved; restored when an approved leave is cancelled.
lifecycle_states: ACTIVE — balance is in effect for the current fiscal year; leave requests can be deducted from it
EXHAUSTED — remainingDays equals 0; no further leave of this type can be approved until more entitlement is accrued or the next fiscal year
CLOSED — fiscal year has ended; balance is archived; a new ACTIVE balance is created for the new fiscal year; transition: close()

business_rules: BR-001 — Date Validity: startDate must be strictly before endDate. A leave request with startDate >= endDate is invalid and must be rejected at submission time.

BR-002 — No Overlapping Approved Leave: An employee cannot have two APPROVED leave requests whose date ranges overlap. Overlap is defined as any shared calendar day between two date ranges. This check applies at approval time, not submission time.

BR-003 — Sufficient Balance: A leave request can only be APPROVED if the employee has sufficient remainingDays in their LeaveBalance for the corresponding policy. The number of leave days requested (inclusive of startDate and endDate) must be <= remainingDays. This check applies at approval time.

BR-004 — Balance Deduction on Approval: When a LeaveRequest transitions from SUBMITTED to APPROVED, the corresponding LeaveBalance.usedDays is incremented by the number of leave days, and remainingDays is decremented accordingly. If remainingDays reaches 0, the balance transitions to EXHAUSTED.

BR-005 — Balance Restoration on Cancellation: When an APPROVED LeaveRequest is CANCELLED, the corresponding LeaveBalance.usedDays is decremented by the number of leave days, and remainingDays is incremented accordingly. If the balance was EXHAUSTED, it transitions back to ACTIVE.

BR-006 — Manager Approval Required: For leave types whose LeavePolicy.requiresManagerApproval is true (annual, sick, emergency), the LeaveRequest must be approved by the employee's manager (Employee.managerId). The approving actor's ID must match the employee's managerId. Self-approval is prohibited.

BR-007 — Minimum Notice Period: If LeavePolicy.minimumNoticeDays is set, the startDate of the leave request must be at least that many calendar days after the submission date. This check applies at submission time. Emergency leave may have minimumNoticeDays = 0 or null, waiving this rule.
